rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 (ki 0.3, kp 2.0, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.5, iteration 2 geometry) is the best result at 97.17. Its gain rests mainly on one oval finish out of 20 trials, with small max_error shifts on the s-bend (0.0613) and slalom (0.0605). Oval steering_oscillation rose from 0.1101 to 0.1253, and line losses stayed at 2 on the s-bend and slalom. The integral lever is therefore real but weakly shown.

Critique points accepted: (1) The rationale now states that the score gain comes from one oval finish and small max_error shifts, not a reliable trend. (2) The success threshold is set relative to the iteration 4 baseline (oval max_error 0.0616, line losses 2 on the s-bend and slalom), not to a fixed 0.06 that sits inside run-to-run spread. (3) The oscillation rule is now per track: the oval baseline is 0.1253 and the 0.16 figure is not used, since slalom and s-bend baselines already sit there. (4) Windup is acknowledged. The contract gives no freeze switch, so I rely on the +/-2 integral bound and check line-loss behaviour after the run. (5) Scale check holds: ki 0.5 at the cap adds up to 1.0 turn unit (about 350 PWM), and the inner wheel stays at 3071 - 1400 - 350 = 1321, so it does not saturate.

Critique points rejected or deferred: the critique argues for returning to ki 0.3 now. I keep ki 0.5 for this race, because the ki 0.3 result already exists and a single test one step further is what separates a real integral effect from noise. The offset hypothesis is still unverified because no signed error is reported; I label it a hypothesis. kd, kp, geometry and base_speed are unchanged so the result is attributable to ki alone. The 3 s finish remains unverified; I do not change speed in this test.

Change from iteration 4: ki 0.3 to 0.5, nothing else.

Expected result (hypothesis): oval max_error at or below 0.061 and line losses at 0 to 1 on the s-bend and slalom, with progress above 0.32 on the oval. Decision rule: if oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.14 (about 12% above the 0.1253 baseline) with no max_error gain, the integral is overcorrecting and the next iteration returns to ki 0.3. If line losses rise above 2 on either s-bend or slalom, ki is too high and is reduced to about 0.4. A finish counts as real progress only if at least 2 of 20 oval trials finish, since one finish in 20 is within noise.
